nodes.summary: Let $N$ and $n$ be natural numbers with $n > 0$, let $\nu, \lambda \in \mathbb{C}$ and $\beta_0, \dots, \beta_{N-1} \in \mathbb{C}$, and let $S = (S_{i,j})_{i,j \ge 0}$ be a $(\nu, \lambda)$-Pascal matrix of size $2n$ with coefficients $\beta$. Then $S_{2n-2,\,2n-1} = 1$.
nodes.title: Corner entry of a nu-lambda Pascal matrix

nodes.summary: Let $N$ and $n$ be natural numbers with $n > 0$, let $\nu, \lambda \in \mathbb{C}$ and $\beta_0, \dots, \beta_{N-1} \in \mathbb{C}$, and let $S = (S_{i,j})_{i,j \ge 0}$ be a $(\nu, \lambda)$-Pascal matrix of size $2n$ with coefficients $\beta$. Then $S_{i,j} = 0$ for all $i, j$ with $i \ge 2n$ or $j \ge 2n$.
nodes.title: Finite support of a nu-lambda Pascal matrix

nodes.summary:
Let $N$ and $n$ be natural numbers with $n > 0$, let $
u, \lambda \in \mathbb{C}$ and $ eta_0, \dots,  eta_{N-1} \in \mathbb{C}$, and let $S = (S_{i,j})_{i,j \ge 0}$ be a $(
u, \lambda)$-Pascal matrix of size $2n$ with coefficients $ eta$. Then for all $i, j < 2n - 1$, $S_{i,j} = \lambda S_{i+1,j+1} + 
u (S_{i+1,j} + S_{i,j+1})$.
nodes.title: Interior recurrence of a nu-lambda Pascal matrix

nodes.summary: Let $N$ and $n$ be natural numbers with $n > 0$, let $\nu, \lambda \in \mathbb{C}$ and $\beta_0, \dots, \beta_{N-1} \in \mathbb{C}$. An array $S = (S_{i,j})_{i,j \ge 0}$ of complex numbers, indexed from $0$, is a $(\nu, \lambda)$-Pascal matrix of size $2n$ with coefficients $\beta$ when the following hold: $S_{i,j} = 0$ whenever $i \ge 2n$ or $j \ge 2n$; $S_{i,j} = -S_{j,i}$ for all $i, j$; $S_{2n-2,\,2n-1} = 1$;…
nodes.title: Nu-lambda Pascal matrix with coefficients

nodes.summary: Let $N$ and $n$ be natural numbers with $n > 0$, let $\nu, \lambda \in \mathbb{C}$ and $\beta_0, \dots, \beta_{N-1} \in \mathbb{C}$, and let $S = (S_{i,j})_{i,j \ge 0}$ be a $(\nu, \lambda)$-Pascal matrix of size $2n$ with coefficients $\beta$. Then for every $j < 2n - 2$, $S_{j,\,2n-1} = \sum_{t=0}^{N-1} \beta_t S_{j+t+1,\,2n-1}$.
nodes.title: Last-column recurrence of a nu-lambda Pascal matrix

nodes.summary: Let $N$ and $n$ be natural numbers with $n > 0$, let $\nu, \lambda \in \mathbb{C}$ and $\beta_0, \dots, \beta_{N-1} \in \mathbb{C}$, and let $S = (S_{i,j})_{i,j \ge 0}$ be a $(\nu, \lambda)$-Pascal matrix of size $2n$ with coefficients $\beta$. Then $S_{i,j} = -S_{j,i}$ for all $i, j$.
nodes.title: Nu-lambda Pascal matrices are skew-symmetric

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
